summary: Throughout the operational years of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), one of the greatest challenges to the development of space travel, settlement on orbital stations, or the dream of living on other planets has been the deterioration of human health in hostile environments unlike Earth. Based on this, Astro Vital was created: a software program that classifies crew health issues and cabin conditions using qualitative and quantitative data organized by a mathematical priority criterion. This helps provide a general overview of crew health problems and can have both terrestrial and space applications.
details: The solution to this problem is based on a mathematical model that takes individual risk levels for each variable to calculate a total risk score. This calculation considers individual hazards, data cross-referencing, the assignment of fixed weights, and the accumulation of information over time, with the goal of detecting risks in both individuals and the cabin. Then it displays it in order of importance, considering how difficult it is to contact Houston being on Mars, and gives what checkup you should do. It is a web in html
